<reason>PRO opened with a vivid, well-structured case (harm lives in the pattern; irreversibility asymmetry) but CON steadily isolated what the motion actually adds beyond existing rules: suspending the accounts that posted nothing locating or threatening. CON landed a real hit in [B2.2] by showing PRO's own opening treated "interesting that she works at this hospital" as harassment before PRO declared workplace criticism "outside the motion," and PRO's repair — a "private-figure target" rider — was convincingly shown to be a contested human judgment that "immediate" deletes. PRO's pressure questions were sharp, but CON answered both directly: the "home alone Thursdays" post is caught by its own content, and the fragment posters are caught by locating-detail rules, with CON honestly conceding the "works there" account stays up. PRO's claim in [A4.5] that "no answer came" was chronologically premature and slightly misleading. PRO's closing pivot (CON also read context) was clever, but CON's reply that the sentence carries its own harm without cluster analysis was persuasive. CON also neutralized the reload argument and pressed "both errors are permanent; only one requires guessing," which PRO never squarely answered beyond restating the appeal point. Clear but competitive win for CON.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 1 [B2.1-B2.5]: exposing PRO's shrinkage from the opening's "works at this hospital" example to "only home addresses," then arguing the motion's marginal reach is exactly the non-threatening accounts, and that botnet-style signals fire equally on viral advocacy — the frame PRO never escaped.</best_rebuttal>
